— The U.S. State Department has approved a $2.1 billion sale of 500 PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE) interceptors for Ukraine's Patriot air defense systems.
The purchase will be funded by Canada, Germany, Norway, and Ukrainian funds backed by the European Union. Lockheed Martin will be the main contractor.
However, the missiles have yet to be manufactured. With the U.S.-Iran war ongoing, Lockheed Martin's production capacity is likely to be focused first on meeting U.S. military requirements rather than supplying Ukraine.
No delivery timeline has been announced.

— Lockheed Martin has published an image of its PrSM (Precision Strike Missile) Increment 4, a long-range missile under development with a planned range of more than 1,000 km.
The missile will be equipped with an L3Harris-developed ramjet engine and a guidance system designed to engage moving ground and maritime targets. It will be launched from M142 HIMARS or M270A2 MLRS launchers.
On September 25, 2026, the U.S. Army awarded contracts to five companies — Anduril, Castelion, Lockheed Martin, Mach Industries, and RTX — to develop and test competing PrSM Increment 4 prototypes during fiscal years 2027–2028.

— The IRGC has released footage showing the interception of U.S. MQ-1C Gray Eagle and MQ-9A Reaper unmanned combat aerial vehicles (UCAVs) over the Strait of Hormuz.
An MQ-1C Gray Eagle was intercepted and destroyed in the early hours of Thursday, October 29, off the coast of Sirik, east of the Strait of Hormuz.
According to the IRGC’s public relations office, the destruction of the MQ-1C brings the reported number of U.S. MQ-1 and MQ-9 drones destroyed by the IRGC’s air defenses to 68, comprising 54 MQ-9s and 14 MQ-1s.
